item_format: Alternative Uses Task: name as many different uses as you can for a common object (e.g., a brick); scored for fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration
tail_discrimination: med - originality scoring separates genuinely creative talent, but inter-rater/scoring reliability is the bottleneck at the high tail
advantage_vs_cogat: captures divergent/creative thinking that CogAT's convergent reasoning items ignore entirely (Renzulli creativity ring); surfaces creatively gifted students a reasoning cutoff misses

item_format: picture-prompted alternate uses for younger children: child sees a familiar object (paper plate) and says as many different uses as possible; scored for fluency and originality
tail_discrimination: low - at ages 4-5 responses are sparse and scoring is noisy, so high-tail separation is weak
advantage_vs_cogat: gives non-readers a creativity signal CogAT never collects; broadens who is flagged for talent development in early grades

item_format: Instances task: 'name all the round things you can think of' (or things that make noise); scored for fluency and category flexibility
tail_discrimination: low - young children's fluency overlaps heavily; weak discrimination at the high end without rich local norms
advantage_vs_cogat: provides an ideational-fluency signal in kindergarten that CogAT does not measure; identifies creative potential before reading fluency exists

item_format: Pattern/Line Meanings: child views an abstract shape or line and names/draws all the things it could be; scored for fluency and originality of interpretations
tail_discrimination: med - figural originality is a distinct talent channel, but scoring reliability limits high-tail precision
advantage_vs_cogat: taps nonverbal figural creativity CogAT never scores; especially valuable for ELL and expressive-language-delayed students (equity)

item_format: standardized verbal creativity battery: ask-and-guess, product improvement, unusual uses, and 'just suppose' word tasks scored on fluency, flexibility, and originality
tail_discrimination: med - normed verbal creativity separates creative talent but carries a high verbal-expression and scoring-reliability load
advantage_vs_cogat: adds a normed verbal-creativity signal absent from CogAT; identifies idea-generation talent a reasoning test cannot

item_format: Consensual Assessment Technique: independent expert judges rate a child's actual creative product (story, invention, drawing) for creativity without a fixed rubric; consensus score = creativity
tail_discrimination: med-high - authentic products can reveal exceptional creativity at the tail, but depend on expert-panel availability and agreement
advantage_vs_cogat: evaluates demonstrated creative output CogAT cannot elicit; captures real-world creative talent, complementing an ability score

item_format: delay-of-gratification wait task: child can take a small reward now or wait to earn a larger one; score = wait time / choice to delay
tail_discrimination: low - wait times are highly context/trust dependent and later replications show weak, attenuated predictive validity once background is controlled
advantage_vs_cogat: observes self-regulation CogAT ignores, but its fragility is a caution: it broadens signals yet must not be over-weighted

item_format: Short Grit Scale (Grit-S): 8 self-report statements on perseverance of effort and consistency of interest (e.g., 'I finish whatever I begin'), 5-point Likert
tail_discrimination: low - self-report ceilings and modest predictive validity (meta-analytic r is small) limit high-tail separation
advantage_vs_cogat: names perseverance/passion (task commitment) that CogAT omits, but as self-report it is a weak, gameable signal best triangulated with behavior/teacher report

item_format: IPIP Conscientiousness self-report items from the Self-Discipline and Achievement-Striving facets (e.g., 'I get chores done right away'), 5-point accuracy scale
tail_discrimination: low - self-report ceilings and social desirability blunt high-tail discrimination
advantage_vs_cogat: measures conscientiousness/achievement-striving that predicts sustained achievement but is absent from CogAT; complements ability with a work-habits signal

item_format: uncertainty-preference behavioral curiosity task: child repeatedly chooses whether to explore certain vs uncertain options; score = threshold of desired uncertainty / exploration of the unknown
tail_discrimination: med - behaviorally distinguishes high-curiosity children and avoids self-report ceilings, though single-session estimates are noisy
advantage_vs_cogat: observes curiosity-in-action that CogAT cannot measure, and does so without reading/verbal load, broadening early identification equitably

item_format: Intrinsic Motivation Inventory (IMI) Interest/Enjoyment subscale: self-report about a specific learning activity (e.g., 'I enjoyed doing this activity very much'), 7-point scale
tail_discrimination: low - enjoyment ratings skew high and ceiling out, giving weak high-tail separation
advantage_vs_cogat: measures intrinsic interest/enjoyment that fuels gifted engagement but is invisible to CogAT; complements ability with drive-to-engage

item_format: portfolio of student work collected over time with student reflections on each piece; reviewed against a giftedness rubric for depth, originality, and growth
tail_discrimination: med-high - sustained high-quality work is a strong tail signal, but rating reliability and unequal home support limit precision
advantage_vs_cogat: documents demonstrated achievement and creativity over time that a one-shot CogAT cannot; NAGC-recommended for surfacing overlooked/young/ELL students

item_format: performance/authentic task scored by rubric: child designs and carries out a short investigation or open-ended product, rated on reasoning, originality, and follow-through
tail_discrimination: med-high - open tasks let exceptional talent show ceiling-free, but demand rigorous rater training for reliability
advantage_vs_cogat: reveals creativity and task commitment in action, ceiling-free, unlike CogAT's fixed items; catches students who underperform on multiple-choice

item_format: self-initiated 'passion project' showcase with a structured reflection on goals, obstacles, and persistence (Renzulli Type III style demonstrated commitment)
tail_discrimination: med-high - depth and follow-through on a self-chosen project strongly signal task commitment at the tail, if authorship is genuine
advantage_vs_cogat: captures sustained task commitment and passion (Renzulli) that CogAT structurally cannot; broadens identification to driven, project-oriented learners

item_format: teacher rating scale (school form) - Motivation and Creativity scales: teacher rates each behavior on a 9-point below/at/above-peer scale (12 items per scale)
tail_discrimination: med - normed, high-internal-consistency scales aid screening, but the Motivation/Creativity scales are weaker discriminators than the Intellectual scale
advantage_vs_cogat: provides normed teacher-rated Motivation and Creativity dimensions absent from CogAT; complements ability testing in a multi-criteria system

item_format: 3x3 array of geometric shapes with the bottom-right cell missing; pick which of 6 options best completes the pattern
tail_discrimination: high - published IRT stats show hard items (e.g. MR.50) carry peak information above +1 SD, sharpening separation near the gifted cut
advantage_vs_cogat: same nonverbal-reasoning family as CogAT Figure Matrices but items are public-domain and IRT-calibrated, giving transparent tail information and cheap fresh forms CogAT cannot supply

item_format: Raven-like 3x3 matrix with one missing cell; select the option consistent with the relational rules running across rows and columns
tail_discrimination: high - stacking multiple simultaneous rules per matrix drives difficulty into the top tail; the 2010 norming data give ready difficulty anchors
advantage_vs_cogat: open, freely regenerable matrices (correlate ~.69-.93 with Raven's) give a CogAT-equivalent nonverbal signal without per-form licensing and with full control of the difficulty ladder

item_format: incomplete 3x3 matrix of abstract colored shapes; identify relationships (shape, color, size, position) and choose the completing tile from distractors
tail_discrimination: high - efficiency (speed x accuracy) peaks in late adolescence, yielding a graded signal that avoids ceiling for able students
advantage_vs_cogat: a purpose-built open alternative to copyrighted matrix tests that exposes item-level reaction-time and accuracy process data CogAT's static booklet cannot

item_format: procedurally generated 3x3 RPM-style matrix with structured rules (constant, progression, arithmetic, distribute-three) across attributes; pick the missing panel from 8 options
tail_discrimination: high - number and compositionality of rules is a direct difficulty knob, enabling items calibrated specifically for the top percentile
advantage_vs_cogat: an inexhaustible, structure-labeled matrix supply with known generative rules, so the tail can be targeted and forms refreshed in ways CogAT's fixed proprietary items cannot

item_format: procedurally generated matrix where relations (progression, XOR, OR, AND, consistent union) act on attributes (size, color, position, number); choose the panel completing the set
tail_discrimination: high - logical relations (XOR/AND) and multi-triple structures create very hard items that discriminate the extreme tail
advantage_vs_cogat: supports held-out generalization regimes, so we can measure genuine rule transfer (not memorized templates), a fairness and robustness edge over CogAT's fixed forms

item_format: matrix-completion items produced from a cognitive model that sets number of rules, abstraction level, and perceptual features to hit a target difficulty (method described, not a fixed item)
tail_discrimination: high - deliberately adding rules and abstraction raises required ability, manufacturing items that bite at the top of the scale
advantage_vs_cogat: a validated blueprint for generating calibrated matrices on demand, letting an in-house bank out-scale and out-refresh CogAT's finite item set

item_format: progressive matrix of geometric patterns with a missing piece; select the option completing it across a wide difficulty range (secure, described only)
tail_discrimination: high - a wide item-difficulty range is explicitly designed to identify giftedness, yet the secure items cannot be extended by us
advantage_vs_cogat: shows the field is already moving to IRT/AIG matrix banks; our edge is an open, ownable version of the same approach with process data and no per-seat licensing

item_format: a row of figures follows a progression on one or more attributes (size up, fixed-step rotation, increasing count); pick the next figure
tail_discrimination: high - simultaneous progressions on multiple attributes (size + rotation + count) sharply separate top reasoners
advantage_vs_cogat: an open, infinitely regenerable series format with tunable tail difficulty and reaction-time data that CogAT does not offer at all

item_format: figural analogy: two figures related by a rule, then a third figure with options; pick the figure completing the analogy (ICAR figural-analogies item type)
tail_discrimination: high - compound transformations (rotate + add + recolor at once) separate the top tail
advantage_vs_cogat: the same analogical construct as CogAT Figure Matrices but from a public-domain resource with open stats, enabling calibrated fresh forms

item_format: five figures shown; select the one figure that does not belong with the others (secure CFIT classification format, described only)
tail_discrimination: high - Scale 3 requires finding TWO odd figures, a documented way to push classification into the high-ability range
advantage_vs_cogat: odd-one-out (violation detection) is a distinct reasoning move CogAT does not isolate; describing CFIT defines the format we can rebuild openly

item_format: several figures share a generated rule except one; pick the figure that breaks the rule
tail_discrimination: high - making the outlier differ on a single subtle attribute among strong distractors bites hard at the tail
advantage_vs_cogat: an ownable, tunable violation-detection task with process data; CogAT has no odd-one-out subtest

item_format: two sets of six figures; the left six all satisfy a hidden rule and the right six violate it - discover which rule distinguishes the sets
tail_discrimination: high - discovering one elegant rule from noisy exemplars is extremely demanding, ideal for the gifted tail
advantage_vs_cogat: measures scientific hypothesis-formation from examples, a higher-order inductive skill entirely outside CogAT's multiple-choice matrix scope

item_format: a few input-to-output grid examples demonstrate a transformation rule; infer the rule and construct the output grid for a new input
tail_discrimination: high - ARC is deliberately hard (few-shot, novel each time), giving strong separation among the most able problem-solvers
advantage_vs_cogat: constructed-response rule discovery with no answer options captures generative reasoning and step-level process data; CogAT is fixed multiple-choice recognition

item_format: RPM-style matrix generated with attribute-balanced answer sets so the correct option cannot be inferred from distractor statistics alone
tail_discrimination: high - removing distractor shortcuts means high scorers must truly solve the rule, tightening tail validity
advantage_vs_cogat: explicitly engineers out answer-set bias, a fairness and validity guarantee CogAT's proprietary distractors cannot document to us

item_format: a partly-filled grid must contain each shape once per row and column; deduce which shape must occupy the target cell from the row and column constraints
tail_discrimination: high - quaternary-complexity items demand integrating many constraints at once, cleanly separating top reasoners
advantage_vs_cogat: measures deductive constraint reasoning (not pattern induction), a distinct Gf facet CogAT never assesses, with a principled complexity dial

item_format: given a spatial condition (e.g. a dot inside the circle but outside the square), choose which of several designs allows that condition (secure CFIT conditions/topology format, described only)
tail_discrimination: high - multi-constraint conditions require careful deduction, contributing strong high-end discrimination in the culture-fair battery
advantage_vs_cogat: condition/topology deduction is a nonverbal logic format absent from CogAT; describing it defines an open rebuild target

item_format: pick the figure that shares BOTH generated attributes (e.g. the same shape count and the same fill) with the target set of three
tail_discrimination: high - requiring two or three co-occurring attributes among tempting single-match distractors bites at the tail
advantage_vs_cogat: a harder, tunable multi-attribute classification with process data; CogAT classification is single-rule, fixed, and secure

item_format: 2D physics sandbox: child draws ramps, levers, springboards and pendulums to guide a ball to a balloon; stealth-scored from solution efficiency, use of physics agents, and telemetry (attempts, redraws, path)
tail_discrimination: med/high - efficiency + novel-solution telemetry separate strong reasoners beyond right/wrong once a level is solved
advantage_vs_cogat: engagement lowers anxiety so children exert full effort and the tail is measured more truthfully; process telemetry captures HOW a child reasons (strategy, revision), which CogAT static items cannot

item_format: tower-defense strategy level (Use Your Brainz, a modified Plants vs Zombies 2): place/upgrade units under resource limits; 32 in-game indicators mapped to 4 facets (analyze constraints, plan pathway, use tools/resources, monitor progress) via Bayesian network
tail_discrimination: high - process indicators (efficiency, foresight, adaptation to failure) correlated with Raven's and MicroDYN and separate strong problem solvers
advantage_vs_cogat: validated against Raven's yet adds real-time process data (planning vs trial-and-error) CogAT never sees; engagement keeps able-but-disengaged children trying, exposing tail ability

item_format: city/ecosystem simulation (SimCityEDU: Pollution Challenge): reduce pollution while keeping jobs/power; player manipulates interacting variables and reads feedback loops; scored with Evidence-Centered game Design against systems-thinking learning progressions
tail_discrimination: high - only strong systems reasoners untangle competing variables; telemetry of interventions vs outcomes discriminates at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: measures dynamic systems reasoning CogAT omits entirely; engagement sustains multi-step exploration and telemetry shows strategy, giving a truer read of gifted systems thinkers

item_format: logic-puzzle sorting game (Zoombinis-style): infer hidden rules to route characters past gatekeepers by attribute combinations; implicit computational-thinking practices (decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, algorithm design) detected from gameplay logs via ML + Bayesian net
tail_discrimination: high - efficient rule inference vs brute force is visible in logs; strong inducers reach abstraction earlier, separating the tail
advantage_vs_cogat: captures the process of induction (how hypotheses evolve) rather than a single figural answer; sustained engagement across grades 3-8 elicits full effort and exposes high-end reasoning CogAT ceilings miss

item_format: first-person 3D physics-puzzle rooms (Portal-style): use portals/levers/momentum to reach an exit; each room is a novel constraint-satisfaction problem; scored from solve time, moves, and solution novelty
tail_discrimination: high - novel multi-step solutions and elegant shortcuts separate strong solvers; low ceiling risk with open-ended rooms
advantage_vs_cogat: Portal-style play produced real gains in problem solving and spatial skill in RCTs; live telemetry reveals reasoning path, and engagement pulls maximal effort from gifted children CogAT would leave disengaged

item_format: figural-matrix puzzle embedded in a quest: complete a 2x2/3x3 pattern to power a machine/unlock a door; distractors generated by automatic item generation; response by dragging the missing tile
tail_discrimination: med/high - depends on including high-difficulty rules and multi-rule items to avoid ceiling; strong inducers solve rare multi-relation items
advantage_vs_cogat: same construct CogAT prizes but delivered without test anxiety and with response-time/first-move telemetry; engagement lets young children show reasoning they would abandon on a paper matrix

item_format: contraption/Rube-Goldberg builder: assemble gears, belts, ramps and switches so a chain reaction achieves a goal; open sandbox scored on solution correctness, efficiency, and originality via stealth indicators
tail_discrimination: high - number and elegance of distinct working solutions expose exceptional mechanical reasoners; open-ended so low ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: measures generative mechanical reasoning and creativity CogAT cannot; engagement sustains long iterative effort and telemetry captures the design process, giving a truer high-end read

item_format: mental-rotation arcade: a target 3D block figure appears; child taps which of several rotated candidates matches (vs a mirror foil); speed+accuracy scored, angular disparity parameterized
tail_discrimination: med/high - include large-disparity and mirror-foil items to avoid ceiling; response-time slope discriminates strong rotators
advantage_vs_cogat: adds response-time chronometry (rotation speed) that CogAT paper items cannot capture; game framing reduces stereotype-threat effects on spatial tasks, yielding a truer estimate especially at the tail

item_format: copy-the-structure block construction (Minecraft-style): reproduce a shown 3D model in a voxel world, or build to spec from an orthographic blueprint; scored on match accuracy, block count efficiency, and rotation moves
tail_discrimination: high - complex occluded or blueprint-only targets separate strong visualizers; open build reduces ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: assesses constructive 3D visualization CogAT cannot present; engagement and telemetry (build order, rotations, error-correction) expose spatial process, giving a richer, truer read of high spatial talent

item_format: fold-the-net mini-game: mentally fold a flat net into a 3D box/shape and tap the correct folded result, or predict where punched holes land after folds/unfolds; difficulty by number of folds and asymmetry
tail_discrimination: med/high - multi-fold, low-symmetry items with plausible foils avoid ceiling and separate strong visualizers
advantage_vs_cogat: same spatial-visualization construct as CogAT surface-development items but with animation scaffolding and RT data; game framing elicits fuller effort, sharpening the high-end estimate

item_format: first-person virtual maze/collectathon (Virtual Spatial Navigation Assessment): explore a 3D building/outdoor world, collect gems, and return to start; scored on route efficiency (time/distance) and map-building behavior
tail_discrimination: high - efficient shortcut-taking vs wandering strongly separates strong navigators; route telemetry is granular
advantage_vs_cogat: measures environmental/large-scale spatial ability CogAT does not touch; rich path telemetry and high engagement reveal wayfinding strategy and true high-end spatial talent

item_format: n-back creature game: a stream of animals/positions appears; tap when the current item matches the one n steps back; n adapts to keep accuracy near target; updating and interference control scored
tail_discrimination: high - high-n and dual-modality variants avoid ceiling and separate exceptional updating capacity
advantage_vs_cogat: directly measures WM updating, an executive construct CogAT does not isolate; adaptive engagement holds attention so the estimate reflects capacity, not boredom, especially at the high end

item_format: sort-and-recall game (List Sorting style): a set of items (animals of different sizes, foods) is shown/named, then the child must report them back in a required order (e.g., smallest to largest); load grows by list length and categories
tail_discrimination: med/high - two-dimension sorts and longer lists prevent ceiling and reveal strong manipulation capacity
advantage_vs_cogat: isolates WM manipulation (not just span) that CogAT does not separate; engaging multimodal delivery yields fuller effort and a truer capacity estimate at the top

item_format: filter-and-remember game (ACE Filter-style): remember only the target-colored shapes while ignoring distractors, then report their orientation/position after a delay; distractor load parameterized
tail_discrimination: high - high-distractor loads separate children who filter efficiently from those who overload; low ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: measures attentional filtering into WM, an executive facet CogAT ignores; engagement sustains attention so scores reflect capacity, and telemetry shows encoding strategy

item_format: running-memory cooking/order game: customers give orders that update; child must serve the last k items in the current order, binding item-to-slot as orders change; running span + binding load scored
tail_discrimination: med - keep binding demands high (multi-feature orders) to avoid ceiling for able young children
advantage_vs_cogat: taps dynamic running-memory and binding CogAT never measures; the playful, concrete task keeps very young children on-task, giving a more valid early-childhood WM read

item_format: multitask drive-and-respond game (NeuroRacer-style): steer a vehicle on a winding road while responding only to specific signs; single-task and dual-task blocks quantify multitasking cost and speed
tail_discrimination: med/high - dual-task cost (not raw speed) separates strong controllers; include high-load blocks to avoid ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: yields multitasking-cost and RT-distribution metrics CogAT cannot; the exciting frame secures full-speed effort, so processing speed is measured at true ceiling rather than under boredom

item_format: flanker fish game: tap the direction the center fish faces while flanking fish point the same (congruent) or opposite (incongruent) way; congruency effect, accuracy and RT scored
tail_discrimination: low/med - flanker effects compress in high-ability children (near ceiling); useful for screening/executive profiling more than top-tail ranking
advantage_vs_cogat: CogAT omits inhibitory control; the game yields a conflict-cost metric and keeps 5-6 year olds attentive, but its low ceiling means it complements rather than extends CogAT's high tail

item_format: crystal-mover puzzle (Tower of London/Hanoi style): rearrange colored balls/crystals across pegs to match a goal in the fewest moves within a move limit; planning time, first-move latency, moves-over-minimum, and rule violations scored
tail_discrimination: high - moves-over-minimum and planning latency on deep problems sharply separate strong planners; low ceiling with hard configs
advantage_vs_cogat: measures planning/executive function CogAT does not; first-move-latency and efficiency telemetry expose whether a child plans ahead or acts impulsively, adding process insight at the tail

item_format: go/no-go stop game: tap fast for 'go' targets but withhold on rare 'stop' signals (or stop-signal variant with a delayed cue); commission errors, RT, and stopping accuracy scored
tail_discrimination: low/med - inhibition compresses at the top; more useful for impulse-control profiling and screening than high-tail ranking
advantage_vs_cogat: adds an impulse-control dimension CogAT lacks; the game keeps toddlers/early learners on-task so inhibition is measured validly, complementing reasoning scores

item_format: narrative emotion-reading game (Crystals of Kaydor-style): as a robot on an alien world, identify and gauge the intensity of facial emotions to complete social quests; empathic-accuracy and calibration scored from choices
tail_discrimination: med - fine intensity discriminations separate highly empathic children; ceiling for basic-emotion recognition, so include subtle blends
advantage_vs_cogat: assesses socio-emotional talent CogAT cannot; narrative engagement yields authentic empathic behavior and process data (accuracy + calibration) that broadens the definition of giftedness

item_format: open-ended sandbox creativity probe: score solution originality and fluency in a design/physics sandbox (e.g., number of distinct working solutions, unusual-but-valid approaches) via stealth indicators
tail_discrimination: med/high - originality metrics can surface exceptional creative talent, but reliability of creativity scoring is a known limitation
advantage_vs_cogat: assesses creativity CogAT wholly omits; a low-stakes engaging sandbox unlocks divergent output and process telemetry, widening identification beyond convergent reasoning

item_format: dot-comparison herd game (Panamath-style ANS): two arrays of animals/dots flash; tap the more numerous set; ratio (Weber fraction) adapts; perceptual controls on size/area; accuracy and RT scored
tail_discrimination: high - finer ratios separate strong number sense; notably, ANS acuity correlates with math even among mathematically gifted adolescents, so it discriminates at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: measures a nonverbal number sense CogAT's quantitative items do not isolate, with minimal language/coaching load; engaging, culture-fair delivery elicits full effort and separates the high-math tail

item_format: adaptive number game (The Number Race-style): choose the larger quantity across nonsymbolic, spoken, and written formats, then move along a racetrack; difficulty adapts on distance, deadline, and symbolic ratio to hold ~75% success
tail_discrimination: med - designed for remediation/low end; raise symbolic ratios, add arithmetic and tighter deadlines to discriminate the high end
advantage_vs_cogat: integrates nonsymbolic-to-symbolic mapping and speed with adaptive engagement CogAT lacks; the always-appropriately-hard loop elicits sustained effort, giving a truer early-numeracy read

item_format: build-the-number puzzle: compose target quantities from base-ten blocks (ones/tens/hundreds) or coins, and decompose/regroup to solve; efficiency of grouping and regrouping strategy scored via telemetry
tail_discrimination: med/high - efficient regrouping and flexible decomposition on large numbers separate strong quantitative reasoners
advantage_vs_cogat: reveals place-value reasoning process (strategy, regrouping) that CogAT's answer-only quantitative items hide; concrete engaging manipulation elicits fuller reasoning from young children

item_format: find-the-word quest (Picture Vocabulary style): hear a spoken word and tap the matching picture from four options; difficulty scales by word frequency/abstractness; low reading load
tail_discrimination: med/high - include rare/abstract words to avoid ceiling and separate strong verbal-knowledge children
advantage_vs_cogat: delivers verbal knowledge assessment with audio (not reading), reducing decoding confounds CogAT verbal items carry; engaging format keeps young/EL children trying, giving a fairer verbal estimate

item_format: interactive story-quest: an audio/animated narrative pauses for choices and comprehension/inference probes (who wanted what, why, what happens next); inference and integration scored from choices and re-listens
tail_discrimination: med/high - deep-inference and integrative probes separate strong comprehenders; ceiling low if inference load is high
advantage_vs_cogat: assesses oral comprehension/inference without reading-decoding barriers CogAT verbal items impose; engagement elicits real comprehension effort, broadening who demonstrates verbal talent

item_format: argument-battle game (Argubot Academy style): build claims and match evidence to support positions, then 'battle' opposing arguments; quality of claim-evidence links scored via Evidence-Centered game Design against argumentation progressions
tail_discrimination: high - constructing strong multi-part arguments and rebutting weak ones separates strong verbal reasoners; open construction lowers ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: measures generative verbal reasoning/argumentation CogAT (recognition-only) cannot; engagement and construction telemetry reveal reasoning quality and true high-end verbal talent

item_format: word-building/anagram treasure game: form as many valid words as possible from given letters, or spell target words, under a time budget; word count/length and lexical-access speed scored
tail_discrimination: med/high - rare/long words and high fluency separate strong verbal children; open production lowers ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: captures productive verbal fluency and lexical access CogAT does not assess; engaging production elicits effortful output and reveals verbal breadth beyond recognition items

item_format: PRECEDENT/PRODUCT: EndeavorRx (AKL-T01, from Project EVO/NeuroRacer lineage) - an adaptive perceptual-motor navigate-and-target game; FDA-cleared to improve attention in children 8-12, validated against the TOVA continuous-performance test
tail_discrimination: low/med - built as a clinical treatment for attention deficits, not to rank high-ability children; tail use would need re-purposing
advantage_vs_cogat: demonstrates that an adaptive game can validly index attention (vs TOVA) with high engagement - a capability CogAT lacks - though as a proprietary treatment it is a precedent, not a reusable item

item_format: decide if two simple figures are the same or different when they differ by one feature (a color or an added dot) and tap YES or NO quickly
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - easy ceiling; only the hardest similarity levels show any high-end spread
advantage_vs_cogat: as a standalone gifted signal it is weak; useful mainly as an engagement/effort check and for response consistency; CogAT captures reasoning but no processing efficiency

item_format: decide whether two number strings (3, 6, or 9 digits) are identical or different and complete as many as possible in 45 seconds per set
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - longer strings add a small working-memory demand that gives slightly more high-end spread than pure pattern matching
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; the added working-memory element is a minor edge, but the honest value is consistency/effort evidence, not peak speed; CogAT has no speeded component

item_format: locate and draw a line through the two identical letter clusters in a row of six, working as fast as possible for 3 minutes (orthographic perceptual speed)
tail_discrimination: low - measures speed of visual symbol discrimination, not reasoning; weak high-end spread
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; describe only; the orthographic angle is reading-linked, not a clean gifted signal; keep as collateral evidence

item_format: look at one target shape, then tap YES if it appears in the row of shapes and NO if it does not, going as fast as you can
tail_discrimination: low - detection speed alone does not separate high-ability preschoolers
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; useful only as engagement/effort and consistency evidence; CogAT is not administered this young in this form

item_format: cross out or tap every target letter (for example every letter d) hidden in rows of similar letters, as fast and accurately as possible
tail_discrimination: low - cancellation indexes attention/speed, not reasoning; poor high-end separation
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; its worth is a sustained-attention/effort read and false-alarm (impulsivity) signal; CogAT captures none of this

item_format: locate and circle a specific repeated pair of pictures as quickly as possible for 3 minutes, ignoring all other pictures
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - the added inhibition/interference control gives marginally more high-end variance than pure cancellation
advantage_vs_cogat: weak alone; describe only; the inhibition component is a small edge, but treat it as collateral executive/effort evidence, not a gifted marker

item_format: on-screen DSST: a 1-9 symbol key sits at the top and the child taps the symbol matching each presented digit; score is correct matches in 120 seconds
tail_discrimination: low - standard speed measure; weak high-end spread
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; use for engagement and response consistency; CogAT gives no speeded/process signal

item_format: match each picture (star, cat, sun) to its partner shape using a small two-row key, tapping as many correct pairs as possible before time runs out
tail_discrimination: low - speed/association only; does not separate high-ability preschoolers
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; value is engagement/effort and consistency at an age CogAT cannot reach in this format

item_format: name aloud, left to right, a grid of familiar repeated objects (ball, dog, star) as fast as possible; score is total naming time and errors
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - RAN predicts reading fluency strongly but is not a broad giftedness marker; more diagnostic of fluency/risk than of the high tail
advantage_vs_cogat: weak as a general gifted signal but genuinely LESS coachable than most speed tasks and a strong early-literacy/fluency predictor CogAT ignores; best as a less-coachable collateral measure (serves H4)

item_format: name a grid of repeated digits (rapid digit naming) as fast as possible; score is completion time and errors
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - alphanumeric RAN predicts fluency well but is not a general high-ability marker
advantage_vs_cogat: weak for the tail; a less-coachable, fluency-linked collateral measure CogAT does not capture

item_format: two vertical lines of different length joined by a bar (a Pi-figure) flash briefly and are then masked; report which side (left or right) was longer; inspection time is the exposure needed to reach a threshold accuracy
tail_discrimination: low-to-med - inspection time correlates about 0.3-0.5 with IQ (stronger in the lower range), so it is a modest, not strong, high-tail discriminator
advantage_vs_cogat: weak-to-moderate standalone; its motor-free design avoids the device/graphomotor confounds of tap tasks, a genuine fairness edge; still treat as collateral evidence, not a gifted cutoff

item_format: scrolling digit-symbol substitution with keyboard or touch input; scores the number of correct matches and the average time per correct match
tail_discrimination: low - a canonical speed measure; weak high-end separation
advantage_vs_cogat: weak standalone; provides per-response timing (a consistency read) CogAT lacks; not a tail discriminator

item_format: infer the rule of a number sequence and supply the next term
tail_discrimination: high - multi-rule and alternating sequences push the ceiling well past grade computation
advantage_vs_cogat: decouples rule induction from arithmetic fluency and logs per-term latency CogAT omits

item_format: 'number machine' input-output task: infer the transformation rule and give the output
tail_discrimination: high - two-step or composite hidden rules separate the top tail
advantage_vs_cogat: rewards rule discovery over calculation and captures hypothesis-testing process

item_format: generalize a growing figural-number pattern to the nth case and justify the relationship
tail_discrimination: high - generalize-and-justify has a very high ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: measures far-transfer generalization and explanation, not a memorized formula

item_format: model two growing quantities and find where they are equal (PISA Apples)
tail_discrimination: high - model-building plus solving equality is strong at the tail
advantage_vs_cogat: prioritizes model-building and relational reasoning over routine computation

item_format: reason about number properties (even/odd, factors) or how to create the largest result
tail_discrimination: high - optimize-and-justify tasks discriminate strongly at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: rewards strategic and deductive number reasoning beyond CogAT rule-finding

item_format: short constructed response: solve and explain a numeric result
tail_discrimination: high - explanation quality separates the gifted tail
advantage_vs_cogat: captures the reasoning-and-justification process CogAT multiple-choice cannot

item_format: enter values to make a relation true or balance both sides of an equation
tail_discrimination: high - multi-unknown and constrained items push the tail
advantage_vs_cogat: targets equation-building and equality reasoning vs CogAT's fixed puzzle format

item_format: multi-step open-response math problem (grade 4)
tail_discrimination: high - multi-step open response is strong at the tail
advantage_vs_cogat: rewards strategy, modeling, and partial-credit process over a single MC pick

item_format: multi-step quantitative reasoning problem (grades 6-8)
tail_discrimination: high - chained reasoning separates top performers
advantage_vs_cogat: measures sustained multi-step reasoning CogAT's short items miss

item_format: nonroutine logic or number puzzle (grades 3-4)
tail_discrimination: high - nonroutine puzzles have a high ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: emphasizes creative nonroutine reasoning absent from CogAT templates

item_format: multi-constraint reasoning sample (grades 5-6)
tail_discrimination: high - constraint satisfaction is a strong discriminator
advantage_vs_cogat: nonroutine constraint reasoning beyond CogAT's item families

item_format: insight-based competition problem (grades 8 and below)
tail_discrimination: high - designed to discriminate the strongest middle-schoolers
advantage_vs_cogat: ceiling far above grade level with genuine insight, unlike CogAT's fixed cap

item_format: Sprint/Target past-competition problem
tail_discrimination: high - Target and Sprint rounds span to the elite tail
advantage_vs_cogat: adds timed multi-step reasoning and speed-accuracy tradeoff data CogAT lacks

item_format: quantitative-comparison format: greater / less / equal / cannot be determined
tail_discrimination: high - the 'cannot be determined' option sharply tests reasoning depth
advantage_vs_cogat: uniquely tests reasoning-under-uncertainty (sufficiency) missing from CogAT

item_format: mathematical-equivalence items (meaning of the equal sign, e.g. 3+4=_+5)
tail_discrimination: high - nonstandard equations reveal deep equivalence understanding
advantage_vs_cogat: diagnoses relational equality reasoning, a known gifted-math signal CogAT misses

item_format: Number Series: determine the missing number in a sequence (Gf/RQ)
tail_discrimination: high - untimed depth reaches a strong tail
advantage_vs_cogat: validated pure quantitative-reasoning measure; adopt as constructed response with latency

item_format: Number Matrices: find the missing number that satisfies a matrix of relations
tail_discrimination: high - dual row/column constraints reach a high tail
advantage_vs_cogat: two-dimensional numeric reasoning richer than CogAT's linear series/analogy

item_format: Figure Weights: choose the weight(s) that keep a balance scale in equilibrium
tail_discrimination: high - multi-substitution items reach a very high tail
advantage_vs_cogat: near-language-free quantitative equivalence reasoning; a strong low-bias signal

item_format: Quantitative Reasoning: verbal and nonverbal number problems and patterns
tail_discrimination: high - adaptive routing already targets the tail
advantage_vs_cogat: a model for an adaptive verbal-plus-nonverbal QR blend beyond CogAT's fixed set

item_format: ratio/rate unit reasoning (e.g., exchange rate, best-buy comparison)
tail_discrimination: high - proportional reasoning is a strong secondary-tail signal
advantage_vs_cogat: adds a multiplicative/proportional reasoning strand CogAT quant omits

item_format: multi-part real-world Problem of the Week reasoning task
tail_discrimination: high - layered parts reach a strong tail
advantage_vs_cogat: adds collaborative, multi-part reasoning and a persistence signal CogAT lacks

item_format: pick which of 4 options is a pure rotation (not a mirror image) of a target 3D cube (Shepard-Metzler) figure
tail_discrimination: high - large angular disparity plus more cubes and added mirror foils cleanly separate top performers
advantage_vs_cogat: CogAT barely measures true 3D rotation (its nonverbal battery is figural reasoning, Lohman 2005); adding it captures STEM talent CogAT misses (Wai/Lubinski/Benbow 2009 SMPY) and is naturally interactive

item_format: a worked example shows an object rotated a given way; pick the option that applies the same rotation to a new 3D object (isometric drawings)
tail_discrimination: high - asymmetric figures and multi-axis rotations resist guessing and stretch the top tail
advantage_vs_cogat: targets rotation-of-rotation reasoning central to engineering and chemistry that CogAT does not isolate; PSVT:R is a documented STEM predictor

item_format: two 3D block figures shown at varying angular disparity; decide same vs different (mirror) as fast as possible
tail_discrimination: high - combining accuracy and reaction time at large angles finely ranks high performers beyond ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: CogAT is untimed figural reasoning and cannot capture rotation speed or efficiency, the hallmark of spatial talent linked to STEM

item_format: card-rotation and cube-comparison items: decide whether pairs of 2D cards or drawn cubes are rotations of the same object
tail_discrimination: high - cube-comparison with hidden faces and oblique views separates advanced visualizers
advantage_vs_cogat: provides pure rotation subscores across 2D and 3D that CogAT collapses into general figural reasoning

item_format: manipulable 3D object family: learner physically rotates an on-screen object with finger or mouse to align it to a target orientation
tail_discrimination: high - fine-grained alignment error and time-to-align yield continuous scores that avoid ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: exploits spatial tasks being inherently interactive; measures dynamic rotation ability CogAT (static, untimed, paper) cannot

item_format: a sheet is folded several times then a hole is punched; pick how the holes are arranged when the paper is unfolded
tail_discrimination: high - three or more folds with multiple punches strongly discriminate at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: a purpose-built folding measure with graded difficulty; CogAT includes folding only as a small reasoning item, not a scaled construct

item_format: advanced multi-fold with multiple asymmetric punches and an oblique fold; choose the exact unfolded hole pattern
tail_discrimination: high - designed for the top tail where symmetric-only foils no longer trip strong students
advantage_vs_cogat: provides discriminating hard items above the typical CogAT folding ceiling to separate the truly gifted

item_format: surface development: given a flat unfolded net with marked edges, pick the 3D solid it forms or match corresponding faces
tail_discrimination: high - many-faced solids with ambiguous nets stretch the top of the distribution
advantage_vs_cogat: measures multi-step visualization (folding a whole surface) that CogAT never assesses as a scaled skill

item_format: incumbent aptitude format: given a 2D pattern with fold lines, pick which 3D object it folds into
tail_discrimination: high - Space Relations is a strong spatial discriminator, but items are proprietary and cannot be refreshed
advantage_vs_cogat: shows a dedicated space-relations construct predicts technical and engineering success; CogAT lacks an equivalent scaled subtest

item_format: form board: shown an outline figure and several shaded pieces, pick which pieces fit together to fill the outline
tail_discrimination: high - many similar pieces requiring mental rotation before placement stretch the top tail
advantage_vs_cogat: assembly and composition is a core visualization factor absent from the three CogAT nonverbal subtests

item_format: incumbent proprietary format: select which several puzzle pieces combine to complete a target shape, done mentally under time
tail_discrimination: high - Visual Puzzles discriminates well, yet items cannot be refreshed or extended by us
advantage_vs_cogat: confirms mental assembly is a distinct visual-spatial index (WISC-V VSI); CogAT has no dedicated assembly subtest

item_format: incumbent proprietary format: arrange red-and-white blocks to reproduce a 2D design under a time limit with speed bonuses
tail_discrimination: high - one of the best-known spatial discriminators; rotation errors flag struggling visualizers
advantage_vs_cogat: establishes block design as a premier visual-spatial index; our public Kohs and TOSA builds capture it without IP limits

item_format: reproduce a colored pattern card using colored cubes (faces are single colors or a diagonal two-color split)
tail_discrimination: high - 16-cube diagonal designs sharply separate strong constructors at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: gives us an ownable, refreshable block-design construct (unlike proprietary WISC) that CogAT entirely omits

item_format: denser maze with many blind alleys; the learner must plan the route before moving to avoid dead-ends
tail_discrimination: high - counting rule-violations and planning time separates methodical top planners
advantage_vs_cogat: probes planful spatial problem-solving that CogAT pattern-reasoning items never touch

item_format: grid route-planning: find the shortest path that visits required targets and reaches the exit in the fewest steps
tail_discrimination: high - optimal versus near-optimal path length is a fine continuous discriminator at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: measures optimization and planning over space, an entirely different and STEM-relevant ability CogAT ignores

item_format: given a map array of objects, imagine standing at one object facing a second and indicate the direction to a third
tail_discrimination: high - large perspective shifts (behind or left) produce fine angular-error gradations at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: perspective-taking is provably separate from mental rotation and is completely absent from CogAT

item_format: worked example on a small scene: point on a response dial to the target as seen from an imagined heading in the array
tail_discrimination: high - continuous angular-error scoring avoids ceiling and ranks the top tail precisely
advantage_vs_cogat: gives explicit measurement of viewpoint reasoning used in navigation and geometry that CogAT omits

item_format: a 3D solid is shown intersected by a cutting plane; pick the 2D shape of the resulting cross-section
tail_discrimination: high - embedded solids cut by oblique planes strongly separate advanced visualizers
advantage_vs_cogat: cross-sectioning predicts STEM (anatomy, geology, engineering) and is entirely missing from CogAT

item_format: interactive: learner drags a cutting plane through a rotating 3D solid, then selects the exposed cross-section
tail_discrimination: high - no-preview oblique cuts of embedded solids discriminate at the very top
advantage_vs_cogat: showcases how a spatial construct becomes an engaging manipulative; CogAT has no interactive or cross-section content

item_format: IRT-calibrated short form: fewer items chosen to span difficulty, each asking for the cross-section of a solid
tail_discrimination: high - IRT design maximizes information near the high-ability cut used for gifted selection
advantage_vs_cogat: delivers efficient, adaptive, tail-focused spatial measurement in a construct CogAT does not assess

item_format: cube comparison: decide whether two drawings of a marked cube could be the same cube shown in different rotations
tail_discrimination: high - hidden-face inference plus larger rotations sharply separates strong 3D visualizers
advantage_vs_cogat: adds occluded-face 3D reasoning central to spatial talent and STEM, which CogAT does not measure

item_format: Public-domain verbal-reasoning item (word relationships/analogy); choose the best completion
tail_discrimination: high - ICAR verbal items are validated to discriminate across the ability range including the upper tail
advantage_vs_cogat: free public-domain pool lets us pre-calibrate and rotate items cheaply; pairing with adaptive vocab-leveling and read-aloud reduces the language-load bias that CogAT verbal carries

item_format: Content-loaded partial analogy across humanities/science/math (A : B :: C : ?), 4 options
tail_discrimination: high - designed for high-ability adults; very strong ceiling / tail discrimination
advantage_vs_cogat: shows a ceiling-rich analogy format; we borrow its rare-relation difficulty but strip the cultural/academic-knowledge dependence using curated grade-normed vocab, which reduces bias relative to a knowledge-loaded analogy

item_format: Given a target word, choose its opposite (antonym) from options
tail_discrimination: med - needs lower-frequency words to reach a high ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: we adaptively level antonym pairs by SUBTLEX frequency and offer oral/picture-supported opposites for young and ELL students, reducing the vocab-exposure bias of fixed CogAT/OLSAT items

item_format: Verbal-comprehension factor markers: produce/select opposites (Opposites Test) and choose the synonym of a target (Vocabulary Test)
tail_discrimination: high - factor-referenced markers span a wide ability range with known psychometrics
advantage_vs_cogat: provides validated factor markers to anchor our vocabulary scale; we then substitute grade-normed low-bias words and oral delivery so the scale is fairer than CogAT's fixed verbal set

item_format: Vocabulary (define a spoken/printed word) and Similarities (explain how two words are alike); young levels use picture prompts
tail_discrimination: high - open-ended responses tap depth and discriminate strongly at the high end
advantage_vs_cogat: captures verbal expression and abstraction that CogAT's multiple-choice format misses; multilingual scoring and picture prompts for young children widen who can demonstrate ability

item_format: Hear/read a short scenario containing an impossibility; identify what is foolish and explain why
tail_discrimination: high - subtle absurdities discriminate strong reasoning and world knowledge at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: adds an inference + world-knowledge check CogAT omits; oral delivery, a picture-absurdity variant for pre-readers, and culturally-neutral scenarios reduce bias

item_format: Read a literary passage; answer inference/interpretation questions (MCQ plus short constructed response)
tail_discrimination: high - interpretive and constructed-response items discriminate at the high end
advantage_vs_cogat: deep comprehension CogAT lacks; adaptive lexile, audio read-aloud, and topic-balanced passages separate reasoning from decoding/knowledge bias

item_format: Read informational text; integrate and infer across the text (MCQ plus short constructed response)
tail_discrimination: high - integrate-across-text items reach the advanced achievement level
advantage_vs_cogat: evidence-based inference with an explicit citing mechanic; adaptive difficulty and read-aloud isolate reasoning from decoding

item_format: Multi-source reading unit (e.g., Rapa Nui): classify statements fact vs opinion, locate and evaluate information
tail_discrimination: high - evaluate-and-reflect items are strong tail discriminators
advantage_vs_cogat: critical-evaluation and fact/opinion reasoning CogAT omits; multilingual passages and oral support broaden access for a fairness-focused screen

item_format: Read a passage; answer inference/main-idea MCQ plus a constructed 'writing to sources' response
tail_discrimination: med-high - constructed 'writing to sources' items lift the ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: comprehension plus evidence-writing (a productive channel CogAT lacks); read-aloud and adaptive passages reduce decoding bias

item_format: Determine the meaning of a word from passage context (meaning vocabulary measured within reading)
tail_discrimination: med-high - low-frequency targets reach the upper range
advantage_vs_cogat: context-based word meaning (vs CogAT isolated words); adaptive target-word frequency and read-aloud reduce vocab-exposure and decoding bias

item_format: Examiner says a word; child points to the one of four pictures that shows it (receptive vocabulary)
tail_discrimination: med-high - low-frequency target words reach high vocabulary levels
advantage_vs_cogat: receptive-only (no reading or expression) lets pre-readers and ELL show word knowledge; pairing with adaptive delivery and home-language receptive norms broadens the pool

item_format: Audio word presented; child chooses which of four pictures best matches; computer-adaptive
tail_discrimination: med-high - the CAT targets ability including the upper range
advantage_vs_cogat: a ready-made adaptive receptive-vocabulary engine for pre-readers; we pair it with home-language norms to reduce ELL bias, something CogAT verbal does not do

item_format: Choose the word most similar in meaning to the target; distractors matched on frequency
tail_discrimination: med-high - can push to low-frequency targets for the tail
advantage_vs_cogat: SUBTLEX equating gives fairer, controllable item difficulty than a fixed CogAT vocabulary set, plus an oral variant for pre-readers

item_format: Given scrambled words, form or identify the correct meaningful sentence
tail_discrimination: med-high - syntactic complexity (embedding, clauses) scales the ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: taps productive syntax CogAT ignores; adaptive syntactic difficulty with reduced rare vocabulary lowers ELL bias

item_format: Evaluate the reliability/stance of sources in a short forum/informational unit; detect author viewpoint
tail_discrimination: high - reflect-and-evaluate items sit at the top of the scale
advantage_vs_cogat: digital critical-evaluation CogAT lacks; multilingual passages and oral support broaden access

item_format: Answer 'why/what should you do' questions about social or practical situations (spoken)
tail_discrimination: high - reasoning plus expression discriminates at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: practical verbal reasoning and expression CogAT's MCQ misses; multilingual scoring broadens who can show reasoning

item_format: Read paired/longer passages; synthesize and infer ACROSS texts (grade 5)
tail_discrimination: med-high - cross-text synthesis items raise the ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: cross-text synthesis (CogAT has no passages); adaptive lexile plus Spanish/read-aloud versions reduce ELL/decoding bias

item_format: Short verbal logical-inference item: deduce a conclusion that must be true from stated facts (public domain)
tail_discrimination: high - validated to discriminate across ability including the upper tail
advantage_vs_cogat: a free calibrated verbal-inference pool; adaptive delivery and read-aloud reduce decoding bias relative to CogAT verbal

item_format: Spoken multi-condition direction acting on a picture grid (e.g., 'tap the star that is above the small tree')
tail_discrimination: med-high - embedded clauses and longer commands stretch the ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: a digitally-adaptive oral-directions task CogAT lacks; the language load is tunable so it is fairer for ELL while still discriminating

item_format: Child hears a digit sequence and must reproduce it in reverse order by tapping numbers, exercising manipulation rather than storage alone
tail_discrimination: high - reversal adds manipulation load and lifts the ceiling well above forward span, separating strong from average
advantage_vs_cogat: adds a manipulation construct plus reversal-error and latency telemetry that CogAT multiple-choice reasoning never captures

item_format: Blocks light up in sequence; child must tap them in reverse order, adding spatial manipulation to storage (backward Corsi)
tail_discrimination: high - reversal load lifts the ceiling above forward Corsi and better separates the high end
advantage_vs_cogat: a spatial manipulation construct plus reversal-error and RT-variability telemetry entirely absent from CogAT

item_format: Colored boxes are searched by touch to find hidden tokens; the child must not revisit a box already found empty or one that already yielded a token - self-ordered search with a strategy measure
tail_discrimination: high - increasing set sizes and a separate strategy score give strong high-end separation
advantage_vs_cogat: yields between-search errors and a search-strategy index (executive process data) that CogAT cannot produce

item_format: A stream of letters appears one at a time; child presses when the current letter matches the one shown 2 items earlier (2-back), continuously updating what counts as the target
tail_discrimination: high - raising n and speed extends the ceiling far past simple spans, ideal for a gifted tail
advantage_vs_cogat: a pure updating construct with hit/miss/false-alarm and RT-variability telemetry; CogAT offers no updating measure and no latency data

item_format: Two simultaneous streams (a moving square position and a spoken letter); child responds separately when either stream matches n items back - dual-modality updating
tail_discrimination: high - dual load produces a very high ceiling that strongly separates the gifted tail
advantage_vs_cogat: a dual-stream updating construct plus rich two-channel error/RT telemetry that CogAT cannot approach

item_format: A list of items streams at a fixed rate and stops unpredictably; child must report the last few (n) items in order, forcing continuous updating of a rolling buffer
tail_discrimination: high - an unpredictable endpoint and fast rates raise the ceiling and index updating linked to fluid intelligence
advantage_vs_cogat: an updating measure validated against fluid intelligence, with per-position accuracy telemetry CogAT lacks

item_format: Item type - any streamed sequence of unknown length where only the last-n must be recalled; presentation rate is tuned to force active updating (slow) versus passive readout (fast)
tail_discrimination: high - fast and long conditions extend headroom for older gifted students
advantage_vs_cogat: one updating paradigm that scales K-8 and emits position-level process data, unlike CogAT static reasoning items

item_format: Alternating processing and storage - child verifies a simple math equation, then sees a letter to remember; after several cycles, recalls the letters in order (automated Operation Span)
tail_discrimination: high - the dual demand yields strong separation and maps onto the latent WM-capacity/gF factor
advantage_vs_cogat: measures WM capacity under interference with processing-accuracy and recall telemetry; CogAT has no dual-task capacity measure

item_format: Child judges whether a pattern is symmetrical (processing), then must remember a highlighted square location (storage); after several cycles, taps the square sequence in order
tail_discrimination: high - visuospatial dual load separates the top end and complements verbal complex spans
advantage_vs_cogat: a visuospatial WM-capacity measure with processing-plus-recall process data absent from CogAT

item_format: Child performs a mental-rotation judgment (processing) then remembers an arrow direction and length (storage); recalls the arrow sequence after several cycles
tail_discrimination: high - combines rotation and span load for strong high-end separation
advantage_vs_cogat: spatial-transformation plus WM-storage telemetry; CogAT figural items are untimed multiple choice with no process data

item_format: Item type - child judges whether each sentence makes sense (processing), then holds a to-be-remembered word/letter (storage); recalls the set in order after several cycles
tail_discrimination: high for readers - the dual verbal load separates strong older students; not suitable pre-reading (K-1)
advantage_vs_cogat: verbal WM-capacity under comprehension load with dual process/recall telemetry CogAT does not collect

item_format: Child is given a few categories (e.g., animals, foods) then sees a stream of words; at the end must report the most recent exemplar seen for each category, discarding older ones
tail_discrimination: med - more categories raises load, but very high ceilings need many categories or fast pace
advantage_vs_cogat: isolates selective updating with per-category error telemetry; CogAT measures neither updating nor error dynamics

item_format: A small grid of digits is shown, then a series of arithmetic operations (e.g., +2) is applied to specific cells; child must track and report each cell final value
tail_discrimination: high - stacking updates on multiple cells pushes the ceiling and taxes transformation
advantage_vs_cogat: an updating-plus-transformation measure with step-level accuracy telemetry CogAT does not capture

item_format: Symbols appear one at a time; child must keep separate running counts of two or more target symbols and report the tallies on demand (symbol-counter)
tail_discrimination: high - tracking three or more counters at speed strongly separates the high end
advantage_vs_cogat: multi-counter updating with per-counter error telemetry; CogAT has no comparable dynamic-load measure

item_format: Item type - a parametric go/no-go where no-go probability and stimulus pacing are systematically varied to titrate inhibitory load across a wide ability range
tail_discrimination: high - rarer, faster no-go trials create the surprise that separates strong inhibitors at the top
advantage_vs_cogat: a titratable inhibition construct with parametric difficulty and error/RT telemetry CogAT cannot match

item_format: Item type - a child fish-flanker where the child indicates the direction of the central fish while ignoring flanking fish; a standardized version spans early childhood
tail_discrimination: med - designed for developmental sensitivity rather than a high gifted ceiling; conflict cost adds some headroom
advantage_vs_cogat: a normed early-childhood inhibition measure with a conflict-cost score CogAT lacks; a model for our own child flanker

item_format: Pairs of digits differ in numeric value and physical size; child must judge one dimension (e.g., which is numerically larger) while ignoring the conflicting dimension
tail_discrimination: med/high - the size-value conflict cost extends discrimination for numerate older kids
advantage_vs_cogat: a numerical interference-cost measure with RT telemetry; CogAT quantitative items are untimed and yield no conflict data

item_format: Item type - child responds quickly to a go stimulus, but on a minority of trials a stop signal appears after a variable delay and the already-initiated response must be cancelled, estimating stop-signal reaction time
tail_discrimination: high - stop-signal reaction time is a continuous latent metric with strong high-end resolution
advantage_vs_cogat: produces a modeled inhibition latency (SSRT) - a process metric CogAT cannot generate

item_format: Item type - across timed subtests the child names shapes/directions against a prepotent response (Inhibition) and holds a body position with eyes closed while ignoring sound distractors (Statue) for younger children
tail_discrimination: med - developmentally graded rather than tuned for a high gifted ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: a standardized child inhibition/self-regulation battery with timed error data CogAT does not collect

item_format: Item type - a timed color-word interference test with an inhibition condition (name the ink color) and an inhibition/switching condition (alternate between naming the ink and reading the word)
tail_discrimination: med/high - the switching condition and completion-time contrasts add headroom for older students
advantage_vs_cogat: separates inhibition from switching via timed condition contrasts - process data CogAT cannot yield

item_format: Item type - the border/advanced DCCS where a border cue on each card signals which rule applies trial-by-trial, forcing rapid cue-driven switching for older preschool/early-primary children
tail_discrimination: high - trial-by-trial mixed switching produces switch-cost variance that separates strong flexers
advantage_vs_cogat: trial-level switch costs and mixing costs - dynamic process data CogAT does not provide

item_format: On each trial a number-letter pair appears; the child does the letter task (vowel/consonant) or number task (odd/even) depending on position, alternating in predictable runs (alternating-runs switching)
tail_discrimination: high - the switch cost (switch minus repeat RT) is a sensitive continuous metric with a high ceiling
advantage_vs_cogat: an explicit switch-cost metric plus repeat/switch RT telemetry CogAT cannot produce

item_format: A cue before each trial tells the child which of two tasks to perform on the upcoming stimulus, so switches occur unpredictably and cue-encoding time is isolated (cued task switching)
tail_discrimination: high - unpredictable cued switches yield large switch and mixing costs that separate the top end
advantage_vs_cogat: decomposes switching into cue-encoding and reconfiguration via RT contrasts - process data CogAT lacks

item_format: Item type - child sorts cards to piles by an unstated rule (color, shape, or number), discovering the rule from feedback; the rule changes without warning, requiring a shift (Berg/Wisconsin card sorting)
tail_discrimination: high - perseverative-error and categories-completed metrics separate flexible high-ability sorters
advantage_vs_cogat: yields perseverative-error and rule-shift metrics (executive process data) CogAT never captures

item_format: Item type - child learns which stimulus feature is rewarded and must shift within a dimension (intra-dimensional) and later across dimensions (extra-dimensional), isolating attentional set-shifting
tail_discrimination: high - the extra-dimensional shift stage is a well-known high-resolution flexibility marker
advantage_vs_cogat: separates within- from across-dimension shifting - a fine-grained flexibility profile CogAT cannot give
